zh: 正事谈毕，酒兴未已，胡雪岩一直对典当有兴趣，此时正好讨教，“福年兄，”他先问：“你是不是典当出身？”“不是。不过我懂，我故世的三叔是朝奉，我在他那里住过一年。”接下来，朱福年便谈了典当中的许多行规和弊端，娓娓道来，闻所未闻。最后似感叹，又似遗憾地说，“当初未曾入典当，自己都不知道是得计，还是失策？因为‘吃典当饭’与众不同，是三百六十行生意中，最舒服的一行，住得好、吃得好，入息优厚，工作轻松，因此吃过这碗饭，别的饭就难吃了！”“照你这样说，如果开爿典当，要寻好手还不容易。”胡雪岩问，“典业中的好手，宾主相得，一动不如一静，轻易不肯他就。是这样吗？”“大致是这样子。不过人材是不断在冒出来的，本典无可位置，另求发展，也是有的。”“那么，我倒要请你留意，有这样的人，我想见见。”这表示胡雪岩也有创办典当的打算，朱福年欣然应诺，而且跃跃欲试地，颇有以半内行作内行，下手一试，以补少年未曾入此业之憾的意思。
en: Their business was settled, but they were still in the mood for drinking. Hu had always been interested in pawnshops, and this was a good opportunity to learn. “Brother Funian,” he began, “did you start out in the pawnbroking trade?” “No, but I know something about it. My late third uncle was a pawnshop appraiser, and I lived with him for a year.” Zhu went on to describe many of the trade’s rules and abuses, speaking so engagingly that Hu heard one thing after another entirely new to him. At last, with something between a sigh and an expression of regret, he said, “I never entered the trade. Even now I cannot tell whether that was a wise decision or a mistake. Earning your living in a pawnshop is unlike any other occupation. Of all the three hundred and sixty trades, it is the most comfortable: good accommodation, good food, generous pay, and light work. Once you have eaten from that bowl, it is hard to stomach any other.” “From what you say, finding good staff to open a pawnshop cannot be easy. An able man who gets on well with his employer is better off staying where he is. He will not readily take another position. Is that right?” “Broadly speaking, yes. But new talent keeps emerging. Sometimes there is no room for advancement in a man’s own shop, and he seeks an opportunity elsewhere.” “Then keep an eye out for me. I should like to meet someone of that sort.” Clearly Hu was considering opening a pawnshop himself. Zhu readily agreed and seemed eager to try his hand, treating his partial knowledge as full expertise and making up for the opportunity he had missed in his youth.

zh: * * *朱福年是在第二天跟吉伯特见面的，那是陈顺生来探问运货舱位消息的时候，也正是由东印度公司转来伦敦总公司发出的何以今年的丝，至今未曾起运的质问之时，所以，吉伯特一见他的面，便先追问恒记和裕记两处的货色，可曾运离上海？“明天就要开船了。”朱福年用英语答说，“吉伯特先生，我觉得我对你有种道义上的责任，必须为你争取最后一个机会。最近商场上有一个大消息，不知道你听说了没有？”“我不知道你指的是什么？”“恒记的东家，也就是我的雇主庞先生，跟胡雪岩在事业上达成了合作的协议，胡雪岩的实力并不充足，但他是商场上一个非常特殊的人物，主要的是他在各方面都有极好的关系，而且他的手腕十分灵活。这两项就是他最大的资本，他所缺少的是现金，而这个缺点，由于跟庞先生的合作而充分弥补了。因此，我可以这样说：胡雪岩是无敌的，没有任何人能够在商场上击败他，包括你吉伯特先生在内。”“我不需要击败他，我只为我的公司的利益打算。最初是我采纳了你的建议，否则，也不至于有今天的僵局。”“吉伯特先生！” 朱福年放下脸来问：“你是不是要讨论这件事的责任？”“不！”吉伯特摇摇头，“那是没有用的。我又不能向你要求赔偿，哪里来的责任可言？你觉得对我有种道义上的责任，足见得你对我还存着友谊，我希望我们仍旧是朋友。”
en: Zhu met Gilbert the next day, just as Chen Shunsheng was enquiring about the shipping space and a demand had arrived from the London head office, forwarded by the East India Company, asking why this year’s silk had still not been shipped. The moment Gilbert saw him, he asked whether Hengji’s and Yuji’s consignments had left Shanghai. “The boats sail tomorrow,” Zhu replied in English. “Mr Gilbert, I feel a moral obligation towards you. I must try to secure one last opportunity for you. There has been important news in the business world lately. Have you heard it?” “I do not know what you mean.” “Hengji’s proprietor, my employer Mr Pang, has entered into a business partnership with Hu Xueyan. Hu’s resources were insufficient, but he is a most unusual figure in business. Above all, he has excellent connections in every quarter and is exceptionally resourceful. Those are his greatest assets. What he lacked was cash, and his partnership with Mr Pang has fully remedied that deficiency. I can therefore say this: Hu Xueyan is invincible. No one can defeat him in business, including you, Mr Gilbert.” “I have no need to defeat him. I am concerned only with my company’s interests. It was your advice I followed in the first place. Otherwise we should never have reached this impasse.” Zhu’s face hardened. “Mr Gilbert, do you wish to discuss who is responsible?” “No.” Gilbert shook his head. “That would serve no purpose. I cannot demand compensation from you, so what is the point of talking about responsibility? Your feeling of moral obligation shows that you still have some friendship for me. I hope we remain friends.”

zh: 听他这一番话，朱福年报之以诚恳的神色，“就因为如此，我要尽我的友谊。”他停了一下，用平静但很坚定的声音说：“吉伯特先生，你并没有失败，一切都可以照你原来的计划实现。但你如果错过此这个最后的机会，那么，你的失败不止于这一次，是明年及以后的日子。用最简单的话说：你将不能在上海买到你所需要的丝。”“照你看，丝价是不是能够减少若干？”吉伯特说，“如果你办得到，我们当然会付你应得的佣金。““不！”朱福年斩钉截铁地说，“决无可能！你应该知道，胡雪岩做生意的精明，是无人可及的，现在他不向你提出延期损失的赔偿，已经是很宽大了。”“好！”吉伯特终于低头了，“我一切照办，只希望赶快订约。”
en: Zhu responded with a look of sincerity. “That is precisely why I want to do what friendship requires.” He paused, then continued in a calm but firm voice. “Mr Gilbert, you have not been defeated. Everything can still go according to your original plan. But if you miss this final opportunity, your failure will extend beyond this one occasion, into next year and the years that follow. To put it simply, you will be unable to buy the silk you need in Shanghai.” “Do you think the price could be reduced at all?” Gilbert asked. “If you can arrange that, we shall of course pay you the commission you deserve.” “No!” Zhu was emphatic. “It is absolutely impossible. You should know that Hu Xueyan’s shrewdness in business is unequalled. He is already being very generous in not claiming compensation for the losses caused by the delay.” “Very well.” Gilbert finally yielded. “I agree to everything. I ask only that we sign the contract quickly.”

zh: 订了约，收银交货，胡雪岩如释重负。但经过一整夜的计算，却又爽然若失，自己都不知道为谁辛苦为谁忙。赚是赚了十八万银子，然而，不过说来好听，甚至于连帐面上的“虚好看”都没有。因为合伙的关系太多，开支也太大。跟尤五、古应春分了红利以外，还要跟郁四再分，付了各处的利息，还要为王有龄弥补海运局的亏空，加上裘丰言和嵇鹤龄那里都要点缀。这一下已经所余无几，却还有开销杭州、湖州、同里三个“门口”所拉下来的“宕帐”，细看一算，除了阜康钱庄的本钱，依旧是一整笔债务以外，还有万把银子的亏空。万把银子在他当然不必发愁，要愁的是这样子费心费力，到头来还闹了一笔亏空，则所谓“创业”也者，岂非缘木求鱼？照道理不应该如此！落到这样的地步，总有个道理在内，当然是自己的做法有了毛病。这个毛病不找出来，令人寝食难安。为此，他虽然一整夜未睡，脑子里昏昏沉沉地，但精神有种异样的亢奋，怎么样也不想上床。
en: Once the contract was signed, payment collected, and the silk delivered, Hu felt a great weight lift from him. Yet after a whole night’s calculations he was left strangely empty, scarcely knowing for whom he had worked and worried so hard. The profit was indeed a hundred and eighty thousand taels, but it only sounded impressive: not even a handsome figure on paper survived. There were too many partners and too many expenses. The profits had to be shared with You Laowu and Gu Yingchun, and then with Yu Si. Interest had to be paid in various quarters; Wang Youling’s deficit at the Sea Transport Bureau had to be made good; Qiu Fengyan and Ji Heling also had to receive their tokens of appreciation. That left very little. There were still the outstanding bills from his three households in Hangzhou, Huzhou, and Tongli. A close reckoning showed that, apart from the capital of Fukang Bank, which remained entirely a debt, he was another ten thousand taels or so short. Ten thousand taels in itself did not worry him. What troubled him was that so much thought and effort should end in a deficit. If that was how he meant to build a business, was he not climbing a tree to catch fish? It ought not to have worked out this way. There must be a reason, some fault in his own methods. Until he found it, he could neither eat nor sleep in peace. Although he had been awake all night and his head was heavy, a peculiar nervous excitement kept him from wanting to go to bed.

zh: 到了快中午时，古应春和刘不才相偕来访，一见了面，古应春失声说道：“小爷叔，你的气色好难看！是不是病了？”刘不才开过药店，对于伤风发烧之类的毛病，也能诊察，当时伸手一探他的额头，又叫他伸舌头出来看了舌苔，很准确地作了判断：“睡得太少，用心过度，是虚火上升。好好吃一顿，舒舒服服睡一觉，精神马上就好了。”“一点不错。”胡雪岩有意将他遣开：“请你替我去约一约庞二，晚上在哪里叙一叙。回头四、五点钟，你到浴德池来找我。”等刘不才一走，胡雪岩将预先一张张计算好的单子，取了出来，捡出古应春的一张交了给他，照胡雪岩的算法，古应春应该分一万五千多银子的盈余。“小爷叔！”古应春略看了一看，将单子推了回去，“第一，你分得我多了，第二，现在不要分，我们仍旧在一起做，商量商量以后怎么个做法，才是正经。”胡雪岩脱口答道：“我正就是不晓得以后怎么个做法？”接着便皱起了眉不断摇头。这态度很奇怪，古应春大为惊疑，“小爷叔！”他很吃力地说，“你好象有啥难言之隐似地。大家自己人，你尽吩咐，有啥‘摆不平’，我的一份不必计算在内。”
en: Towards noon, Gu Yingchun and Liu Bucai came together. The moment Gu saw him, he exclaimed, “Little Uncle, you look dreadful! Are you ill?” Liu had once run a pharmacy and could diagnose such ordinary ailments as colds and fevers. He felt Hu’s forehead, asked him to put out his tongue, examined its coating, and gave a very accurate diagnosis. “Too little sleep and too much mental exertion. Deficiency heat is rising. Eat a good meal and have a comfortable sleep, and you will feel yourself again.” “Exactly.” Hu deliberately found a reason to send him away. “Please arrange for me to meet Pang somewhere this evening. Come and find me at Yudechi Bathhouse at four or five.” Once Liu had left, Hu brought out the individual statements he had calculated beforehand and handed Gu his. According to Hu’s reckoning, Gu was entitled to a profit of more than fifteen thousand taels. Gu glanced through it and pushed it back. “Little Uncle, first, you have allotted me too much. Second, let us make no distribution now. We shall go on working together. What matters is to discuss how we should proceed.” “That is precisely what I do not know!” Hu blurted out, frowning and shaking his head repeatedly. His strange manner startled Gu. With some difficulty, he said, “Little Uncle, you seem to have some trouble you find hard to speak about. We are all friends. Tell me what you need. If there is anything you cannot settle, leave my share out of the reckoning.”

zh: “应春兄！”胡雪岩相当感动，率直答道：“我一无所得，就是朋友的情分义气，千金不换。”“岂止于千金不换？小爷叔，你不要说一无所得，在我看，所得正多。不说别的，只说朱福年好了，庞二虽有些大少爷的脾气，有时讲话不给人留情面，到底御下宽厚，非别的东家好比，可是朱福年还是有二心，只有遇到小爷叔你，化敌为友，服服帖帖，这就是你的大本事，也就是你的大本钱。“由于说得中肯，不是一般泛泛的恭维可比，所以胡雪岩听了这几句话，深受鼓舞，“老古，”他便索性问道：“你直言谈相，看我做生意有啥毛病要改？”
en: Deeply moved, Hu answered frankly, “Brother Yingchun, I have gained nothing—except the loyalty and affection of friends, which a fortune could never buy.” “Worth more than any fortune! But do not say you have gained nothing, Little Uncle. To my mind you have gained a great deal. Take Zhu Funian alone. Pang has something of a pampered young gentleman’s temper and sometimes speaks without sparing anyone’s feelings, but he is generous to his staff in a way few employers are. Yet Zhu still harboured disloyal intentions. Only when he encountered you did an enemy become a friend and submit completely. That is your great ability and your great capital.” These observations went to the heart of the matter; they were far more than empty compliments. Hu was greatly encouraged. “Old Gu,” he asked outright, “speak frankly. What faults do you see in the way I do business? What should I change?”

zh: “毛病是谈不到。不过，小爷叔，中国人有句话，叫做‘业精于勤，荒于嬉’，这个‘勤’字照我讲，应该当做敬业的敬，反过来‘嬉’字不作懒惰解释，要当作浮而不实的不敬来讲。敬则专，专心一志，自然精益求精。小爷叔，如果说你有失策之处，我直言谈相，就是不专心。“古应春又说，”人的精力到底有限，你经手的事情到底太多了，眼前来看，好象面面俱到，未出纰漏，其实是不是漏了许多好机会，谁也不得而知。“他一路说，胡雪岩一路点头，等他说完，随即答道：“有好几位都这样劝过我，不过没有你说得透彻。我刚才在想，忙了半天，两手空空，总有个毛病在那里，你说我不专心，这就是我的毛病。不过，也不能说两手空空……”他没有再说下去，说下去怕古应春多心，他本人两手空空，还亏下了帐，但相交合作的朋友，都有好处。这盘帐要扯过来算，还是有成就的。
en: “I would not call them faults. But there is a Chinese saying: ‘A calling is mastered through diligence and ruined by play.’ I take ‘diligence’ to mean respect for one’s calling. And ‘play’, in turn, means not laziness but a shallow lack of seriousness. Respect brings concentration; single-minded concentration brings continual improvement. Little Uncle, if you have made a mistake, I must tell you plainly that it is a lack of concentration. A man’s energy is limited, after all, and you have far too many affairs in hand. For the moment, everything seems to be attended to and nothing has gone wrong. Yet who can say how many good opportunities you may have missed?” Hu nodded throughout. When Gu had finished, he immediately replied, “Several people have advised me along these lines, but none has explained it as clearly as you. Just now I was thinking that after all this effort I was left empty-handed. There must be something wrong. You say I lack concentration. That is my fault. Still, I cannot really say I am empty-handed…” He stopped, afraid that saying more might make Gu uneasy. He himself had nothing to show for his work and was even in debt, but all the friends who had worked with him had benefited. Viewed from that side of the ledger, he had achieved something after all.

zh: 这样转念，更觉精神一振，“走，走，”他站起身来说：“照刘三爷的话，好好吃它一顿，睡它一觉。有没有什么好番菜？吃完了到浴德池去泡它一下午。”“好番菜是有，只怕你吃不来。”“怎么吃不来？”“夏天讲究吃‘色白大菜’，生冷清淡，半生不熟，吃不惯的会倒胃口。”“那就算了。还是……”“还是到我这里去吃饭吧！七姐现在返璞归真了，到处跟人学做菜，今天在做粉蒸鸡，还有你们西湖上的莼菜……”“你不要再说了。”胡雪岩咽了口唾沫答道，“再说下去，我真要流口水了。”于是一起到古应春那里。七姑奶奶果然卷起衣袖，在厨房里大忙特忙，汗水蒸润，她那张银盆似的脸，和两条藕也似的手臂，格外显得红白分明，看见胡雪岩在厨房门口探头一望，赶紧喊道，“厨房里象火焰山一样，小爷叔，快不要进来！”“我饿了！”胡雪岩老实答说，“有啥吃的，先弄点来喂喂我。”“我先下碗米粉干，让你点点饥。回头慢慢吃酒。”等一碗鸡汤火腿笋干米粉下肚，接着便摆桌子喝酒，恰好尤五也到了，胡雪岩越有兴致。
en: The thought revived him further. “Come, come!” He rose. “We shall follow Third Master Liu’s advice: a good meal and a good sleep. Is there any good Western food to be had? Afterwards we can spend the afternoon soaking at Yudechi.” “There is, but I am afraid you might not like it.” “Why should I not?” “In summer the fashionable thing is a se-bai Western dinner: cold, lightly flavoured food, raw or only half cooked. It can turn your stomach if you are not used to it.” “Then forget it. We had better…” “We had better eat at my place. Seventh Sister has returned to simpler ways. She is learning to cook from everyone she meets. Today she is making chicken steamed with rice meal, and there is water shield from your own West Lake…” “Say no more!” Hu swallowed. “If you go on, I shall start drooling.” They went together to Gu’s house. Sure enough, the Seventh Lady had rolled up her sleeves and was busy in the kitchen. The heat had brought a sheen of perspiration to her round, silver-basin face and her lotus-root arms, making their pink and white all the more vivid. Seeing Hu peer through the kitchen doorway, she called at once, “It is like the Flaming Mountain in here! Do not come in, Little Uncle!” “I am hungry,” he replied honestly. “Whatever you have, give me something to eat first.” “I shall cook a bowl of rice noodles to take the edge off your hunger. Then we can have a leisurely drink.” He finished a bowl of rice noodles in chicken broth with ham and dried bamboo shoots, and the table was set for wine. You Laowu happened to arrive as well, putting Hu in still better spirits.

zh: 席间当然要问他今后的打算，胡雪岩却反问尤五和古应春，要怎么样打算，才能于大家有益？“这话就是很难说了。”尤五答说，“照我的心思，最好你别人的闲事都不管。”“五哥也是！”七姑奶奶性子直，马上就补了一句他未曾说出来的话：“别人的闲事不要管，只管你的事。是不是？”大家都笑了。“这当然是一厢情愿。不过，”尤五正色说道，“我们漕帮方面，生路越来越狭，小爷叔，你答应过的，总要替我们想个办法。”“当然，当然。我一定当我自己的事来办。”胡雪岩又问古应春：“你看呢，我以后该怎么做法？”“我刚才就说过了。”胡雪岩点点头，重新回想他上午所作的那番劝告。那些话，尤五和七姑奶奶并不知道，尤其是七姑奶奶性子急，便追问首，胡雪岩将古应春劝他专心的话，说了给她听，并且盛赞古应春看得深，识得透。
en: Naturally they asked about his plans, but he put the question back to You and Gu: what course would benefit everyone? “That is difficult to say,” You replied. “If I had my way, you would leave everyone else’s affairs alone.” “Just listen to Brother Five!” The Seventh Lady was direct by nature and at once supplied the words he had left unsaid. “Leave everyone else’s affairs alone and attend only to yours. Is that it?” Everyone laughed. “Of course that is only wishful thinking on my part,” You said. Then he grew serious. “But the ways of earning a living are narrowing for our grain-transport brotherhoods. You promised, Little Uncle. You must find a way for us.” “Certainly, certainly. I shall treat it as my own business.” Hu turned to Gu. “And what do you think I should do?” “I told you just now.” Hu nodded, recalling the advice Gu had given him that morning. You and the Seventh Lady had not heard it. Impatient as ever, she pressed him for an explanation, and he repeated Gu’s counsel about concentrating his efforts, warmly praising its insight and clarity.

zh: “谢谢一家门！”七姑奶奶撇着嘴说，“小爷叔，他是狗头军师，你不要听他的话。”古应春不服气，但也不敢跟她争辩，只说：“小爷叔，‘妇人之言，慎不可听’。”“啥叫‘妇人之言’？”七姑奶奶的反应快得很，“场面总是越大越好。照你的说法，有皇帝做也不要做了，因为管的事太多太杂？“一句话驳得古应春哑口无言，摇摇头轻轻说了句：“歪理十八条。”胡雪岩看他那无奈七姑奶奶之何的尴尬神态，未免好笑，但一向不以他那个“宝贝妹子”为然的尤五，却帮着她说话：“阿七说的倒也不是歪理。事情不怕多，要有人管，皇帝好做，难的是用不着一个好宰相。小爷叔，我想，考古的话也不错，阿七的比喻也有道理，你是聪明人，不妨拿他们两个人的话好好想一想，作一番打算。““是的！”胡雪岩深深点头。于是他一面吃喝闲谈，一面在心中盘算，等酒醉饭饱，他的盘算也大致停当了。
en: “Thanks to him and his entire family!” The Seventh Lady curled her lip. “Little Uncle, he is a bungling strategist. Do not listen to him.” Gu disagreed but dared not argue with her. He merely said, “Little Uncle, ‘Take care never to heed a woman’s words.’” “What do you mean, ‘a woman’s words’?” she retorted instantly. “Surely the larger your sphere of activity, the better. By your reasoning, a man should refuse to be emperor because he would have too many different affairs to manage!” That left Gu without an answer. He shook his head and murmured, “Eighteen varieties of crooked reasoning.” Hu was amused by Gu’s helpless embarrassment. You, however, who usually took a dim view of his precious younger sister, now supported her. “What Seventh Sister says is not altogether unreasonable. There is no harm in having many affairs, provided there are people to manage them. Being emperor is easy; the difficulty is finding a good chief minister. Little Uncle, I think Old Gu is right, but Seventh Sister’s comparison also makes sense. You are a clever man. Think over what they have both said and work out a plan.” “Yes.” Hu nodded gravely. As he ate, drank, and chatted, he kept turning the matter over. By the time he had enjoyed enough wine and food, his plan was largely settled.

zh: “五哥，老古！”他说，“我们先把帐分了……”“不必分！”尤五抢着说，他的意思跟古应春一样，主张就原来的资本和盈余，听候胡雪岩全权运用，能够“利上滚利”。“我懂你们的意思。”胡雪岩说，“我要重起炉灶，做几样事业，大家分开来管，我只抓个总。就好比做皇帝一样，要宰相大臣分开来办事，用不着我亲自下手。”“嗯，嗯！”在座的三个人，不约而同地颔首表示同意。“第一样是钱庄，这方面是我的根本，我也内行，恐怕还是要亲自下手。第二样是丝，在湖州，我交给陈世龙，在上海，我交给老古。““好的！”古应春说，“我当仁不让，无需客气。将来茶叶、桐油也好做洋庄，慢慢儿再说。”“将来销洋庄都归你一手担当。茶叶、桐油我也想过，只要你认为可以做，我无不赞成。不过眼前新丝就要上市了，所以要请你赶紧筹划，专心一致，百事不管。不过……”胡雪岩看一看七姑奶奶，笑笑不再说下去。
en: “Brother Five, Old Gu,” he began, “first let us divide up the accounts…” “There is no need!” You interrupted. His view was the same as Gu’s: the original capital and the profits should remain entirely at Hu’s disposal, to earn profit upon profit. “I understand,” Hu said. “But I want to make a fresh start, with several businesses managed separately by different people, while I take overall charge. Like an emperor, I shall have ministers handling their own affairs without needing to do everything myself.” All three listeners nodded their agreement. “First comes banking. That is my foundation, and I know the trade, so I shall probably still have to attend to it myself. Second comes silk. In Huzhou I shall put Chen Shilong in charge; in Shanghai, Old Gu.” “Good,” Gu replied. “I shall accept that responsibility without standing on ceremony. Later we can also export tea and tung oil. We can discuss those in due course.” “All our exports will be in your hands. I have thought about tea and tung oil too. If you think they are worth doing, I shall support you. But the new silk will soon be on the market, so you must begin planning at once. Concentrate entirely on that and leave everything else alone. Except…” He glanced at the Seventh Lady and stopped with a smile.

zh: 这大有皮里阳秋的意味，七姑奶奶免不了要问：“小爷叔，不过什么？”“不过，”胡雪岩笑道，“百事不管，你们的终身大事是非管不可的。我也是这样子，别样闲事不能再管，你的这桩大事，非效劳到底不可。当着五哥在这里，我做大媒的说一句，你们挑日子、办喜事，乾坤两宅，自己商量，不必我来传话。古家老族长那里的归我疏通，一定不会办不通，你们放心好了。““是的。”尤五点点头说，“这件事，我就这几天要好好谈一谈。现在且不去说它，小爷叔你再讲你的打算。”
en: There was plainly something behind the remark, and the Seventh Lady could not help asking, “Except what, Little Uncle?” “Except,” Hu answered, laughing, “that however much you leave everything else alone, your marriage must be attended to. The same goes for me. I can no longer concern myself with every other matter, but I must see this one through for you. With Brother Five here, let me say this as your chief matchmaker: choose a day and arrange the wedding. The bride’s and bridegroom’s families can discuss it directly without having me carry messages between them. I shall bring the Gu family’s old clan head round. I am certain it can be done, so set your minds at rest.” “Yes,” You said, nodding. “We must have a proper talk about it in the next few days. But let us leave it for now. Go on with your plans, Little Uncle.”

zh: “我还打算办两样事业，一样是典当，一样是药店。药店请刘三爷来做，典当，我想跟庞二谈一谈，请朱福年帮我的忙。”对他的这番打算，尤五和古应春默然不置可否，这意思就是不以为然，在古应春觉得他不宜做此自己不懂的事业，而刘不才的本性，也不宜于苦干创业，朱福年则相交未几，虽说“南蛮不复反矣”，但他究竟有几许本事，尚未明了，何以轻付以重任？尤五也略有这样的想法，此外他还有疑虑，率直问道：“小爷叔，一样钱庄，一样丝，都是大本钱，你哪里还有余力开当铺、开药店？”“五哥说到要害上来了。”胡雪岩很起劲地，“自然我都有打算。”胡雪岩的打算，是凭他的信誉、本领，因人成事。阜康设分号，是庞二有过承诺，愿意支持的，做丝生意，仍旧是大家集股。开典当的本钱，他看中了苏州潘叔雅那班富家公子，开药店则预备在江浙官场上动脑筋。
en: “I also intend to start two other businesses: a pawnshop and a pharmacy. I shall ask Third Master Liu to run the pharmacy. As for the pawnshop, I want to speak to Pang and ask for Zhu Funian’s help.” You and Gu offered neither approval nor objection. Their silence meant that they did not agree. Gu thought Hu should not enter trades he did not understand. Liu Bucai’s temperament was also ill suited to the hard work of establishing a new business. As for Zhu, they had known him only a short time. Though they might now say of him, “The southern barbarians will never rebel again,” his actual abilities were still uncertain. How could such important responsibilities be entrusted to him so readily? You had similar thoughts and another doubt besides, which he expressed frankly. “Little Uncle, banking needs a great deal of capital, and so does silk. Where will you find the means to open a pawnshop and a pharmacy as well?” “Brother Five has put his finger on the point,” Hu said eagerly. “Naturally I have made plans.” His plan was to use his reputation and ability to enlist other people’s help. Pang had promised support for a Fukang branch, while the silk business would continue to be financed by pooled shares. For the pawnshop’s capital, he had his eye on Pan Shuya and the other wealthy young gentlemen of Suzhou. For the pharmacy, he intended to find a way through official circles in Jiangsu and Zhejiang.

zh: “我再说，为啥要开典当、开药店？这两样事业，一时都无利可图，完全是为了公益，我开典当是为方便穷人。胡雪岩三个字，晓得的人，也不算少了，但只有做官的和做生意的晓得，我以后要让老百姓都晓得，提起胡雪岩，说一声：这个人不错！事业就会越做越大。为此，我要开药店，这是扬名的最好办法。再说，乱世多病痛，大乱之后，必有瘟疫，将来药店的生意，利人利己，是一等一的好事业。“听得这一说，七姑奶奶首先就钦佩不止，“你听听，”她带点教训意味地对古应春说：“小爷叔的眼光，才真叫眼光！看到大乱以后了。你要学学小爷叔。”“本来就跟小爷叔在学。”古应春转脸问道，“小爷叔，你说开药店的本钱，出在公家，是怎么个办法？”“ 这要靠关系了。军营里自然要用药，我要跟刘三爷商量，弄两张好方子，真材实料修合起来，譬如刀伤药、诸葛行军散、辟瘟丹之类，要一服见效，与众不同。这样子就好禀请各路粮台，先定我们多少，领下价款来做本钱。”“真是！”七姑奶奶听得眉飞色舞，“我看世界上，没有小爷叔没有办法的事！”“七姐，”胡雪岩有些惶恐，“这话捧得我太过分了。一个人的力量到底有限，就算三头六臂，也办得了多少事？要成大事，全靠和衷共济，说起来我一无所有，有的只是朋友。要拿朋友的事当自己的事，朋友才会拿你的事当自己的事。没有朋友，就是有天大的本事，也还是没有办法。”
en: “Let me explain why I want a pawnshop and a pharmacy. Neither will make a profit immediately. I mean them entirely for the public good. A pawnshop will help poor people. Quite a few people already know the name Hu Xueyan, but they are all officials and businessmen. In future I want ordinary people to know it too. When they hear my name, I want them to say, ‘That is a decent man!’ Then my businesses will keep growing. That is why I want a pharmacy: it is the best way to make a name. Besides, troubled times bring illness, and great upheavals are always followed by epidemics. A pharmacy will benefit others and ourselves. It is one of the best businesses there is.” The Seventh Lady was the first to express her admiration. “Listen to him,” she told Gu, with a touch of admonition. “That is real foresight! Little Uncle is already looking beyond the war. You ought to learn from him.” “I am learning from him.” Gu turned to Hu. “You said the pharmacy’s capital would come from public funds. How would that work?” “Through our connections. The army must have medicines. I shall discuss it with Third Master Liu and get a couple of good prescriptions, then prepare them properly with genuine ingredients—wound medicine, for instance, Zhuge Marching Powder, or Biwen Pills. They must work with a single dose and stand apart from ordinary remedies. Then we can ask the various army supply offices to place advance orders and use their payments as capital.” The Seventh Lady was delighted. “Really! I do not believe there is anything in the world Little Uncle cannot find a way to do!” Hu was a little alarmed. “Seventh Sister, that is far too much praise. A single man’s strength is limited. Even with three heads and six arms, how much could he do? Great undertakings depend entirely on people working together. You might say I have nothing except friends. Only if you treat your friends’ affairs as your own will they treat yours as theirs. Without friends, the greatest ability in the world will still get you nowhere.”

zh: “小爷叔这话一针见血，”尤五紧接着他的话说，“我们那一伙弟兄，都当小爷叔好朋友，现在等着你老发号施令呢！”“你别忙！我答应替你们筹出一条生路来，一定要做到，说句老实话，我眼前第一件大事，就是替你们去开路，大致的办法，我已经有了……”这是胡雪岩另一项与民生国计有关的大事业，他准备利用漕帮的人力、水路上的势力跟现成的船只，承揽公私货运，同时以松江漕帮的通裕米行为基础，大规模贩卖粮食。“乱世米珠薪桂，原因有好多，要一样样去考究。兵荒马乱，田地荒了，出产少了，当然是一个原因，再有一个原因是交通不便，眼看有米的地方因运不出，卖不掉，多么可惜！这还不算，最可惜的是糟蹋掉了！有些人家积存了好多粮食，但打起仗来，烧得光光，或者秋收到了，战事迫近，有稻无人割，白白作践。能够想办法不糟蹋，你们想，于公于私多么好！”“有道理！”尤五矍然而起，“前面两个原因，我懂，后面说的这一层道理，我还是第一次听到。倒要请教小爷叔，怎么样才能不糟蹋？”“这就要看局势了。眼要明，手要快，看啥地方快靠不住了，我们多调船过去，拿存粮抢运出去。能割的稻子，也要抢着割下来。”胡雪岩又说：“这当然要官府帮忙，或者派兵保护，或者关卡上格外通融，只要说好了，五哥，你们将来人和、地利都具备，是独门生意。”
en: “You have struck the nail on the head, Little Uncle,” You said at once. “All our brothers regard you as a good friend. They are waiting for your orders.” “Not so fast! I promised to find a livelihood for you, and I shall keep that promise. To tell you the truth, opening that path is my most urgent business. I already have the outline of a plan…” This was another major undertaking affecting both the people’s livelihood and the country’s economy. Hu intended to use the grain-transport brotherhoods’ manpower, influence along the waterways, and existing boats to carry government and private cargo. At the same time, he would use the Songjiang brotherhood’s Tongyu Rice Shop as the basis for a large grain business. “There are several reasons why rice costs as much as pearls and firewood as much as cassia in wartime. We must examine them one by one. Fighting leaves fields untended and reduces production: that is one reason. Another is the difficulty of transport. How wasteful it is when places have rice but cannot move it out or sell it! But there is something more wasteful still: grain destroyed outright. Some households have large stores, only to see them burned in the fighting. Or autumn comes and the war draws near: rice stands ready in the fields, but there is no one to cut it, and it is wasted. If we could prevent that waste, think what a benefit it would be to the public and to ourselves!” “That makes sense!” You sprang up. “I understand the first two reasons, but I have never heard this last point made before. Tell me, Little Uncle, how can we prevent the waste?” “By watching the situation. We must see clearly and act quickly. When a place is becoming unsafe, we send plenty of boats and get its stored grain out in time. Any rice ready for cutting must be harvested quickly too. Of course we shall need official help: troops to protect us, perhaps, or special accommodation at the checkpoints. Once it is all arranged, Brother Five, you will have both the cooperation of your people and the advantages of the waterways. No one else could match the business.”

zh: 尤五和古应春都不作声，两个人将胡雪岩的话，细细体味了一会，才大致懂得了他的做法。这确是一项别人所抢不去的好生意，但是做起来不容易。“官场的情形，小爷叔你晓得的，未见得肯帮我们的忙。”“一定肯！只看怎样说法？其中还有个道理：打仗两件事，一是兵，二是粮，叫做足食足兵。粮食就这么多，双方又是在一块地方，我们多出一分粮食，长毛就少一分粮食，一进一出，关系不轻。所以，我去一说这层道理，上头一定会赞成。”“ 对！”尤五问道：“小爷叔你预备跟哪个去说？王大老爷？”“是的。我先跟他去说。事不宜迟，明天我就走！我还有好多法子可以治长毛，譬如加紧缉私，断绝他们的日用百物的供应之类。”胡雪岩站起身来，很起劲地挥着手：“做小生意迁就局势，做大生意先帮公家拿局势扭过来。大局好转，我们的生意就自然有办法。你们等着，看我到了杭州，重起炉灶，另有一番轰轰烈烈的事业。”
en: You and Gu were silent. They considered Hu’s words carefully before grasping the broad outline of his method. It was indeed an excellent business that no one else could wrest from them, but carrying it out would not be easy. “You know how officials are, Little Uncle. They may not be willing to help.” “They certainly will! It all depends on how the case is put. There is another reason: war requires two things, troops and grain—enough food and enough soldiers. There is only so much grain, and both sides are in the same area. Every measure we gain is one the Taipings lose. The effect on both sides is considerable. Once I explain that, the authorities are bound to approve.” “Exactly!” You asked, “Whom do you intend to speak to? Prefect Wang?” “Yes, I shall speak to him first. There is no time to lose. I leave tomorrow! I have plenty of other ways to deal with the Taipings, such as tightening the suppression of smuggling and cutting off their supplies of everyday necessities.” Hu stood up and waved his hand with enthusiasm. “Small traders adapt themselves to circumstances. A businessman on a large scale first helps the government change the circumstances. Once the overall situation improves, our business will find its way. Just wait. When I reach Hangzhou, I shall make a fresh start and launch undertakings that will really stir the world.”

zh: （本篇终）
en: End of this part.

zh: 至此，胡雪岩依靠官府、利用漕帮、结识外商买办、网罗赌徒、拉拢富商，终于发迹于战乱的年代，在上海、杭州立足。
en: By this point, Hu Xueyan has relied on official support, made use of the grain-transport brotherhoods, established connections with foreign merchants and compradors, recruited gamblers, and cultivated wealthy businessmen. He has at last risen to prosperity in an age of war, establishing himself in Shanghai and Hangzhou.

zh: 此后，高阳先生在《红顶商人》和《灯火楼台》等书中，依然以其丰富的历史知识和深厚的写作功力，铺叙了胡雪岩自上海、杭州发迹后，资财逐渐过于鼎盛之势，而最终归于破产的过程。书中说道，身为江浙大贾的胡雪岩，运饷粮助清军解杭州之围，城破，即转倚左宗棠为靠山，为其筹措军饷，购运西洋新式枪炮，借巨资于洋商，助左宗棠西征并协大办洋务；继而倚仗官府，扩充实力，操纵了江浙商业，声名盛于东南，直至身受二品顶戴，获赏穿黄马褂、紫禁城骑马的殊荣，赫赫然成为晚清唯一顶红顶子的商人；胡雪岩穷奢极侈、酷好女色，在上海、杭州等地，营造多处富丽宅园，姬妾成群，荒淫无度，以为乐事，十数年间，财势鼎盛至极；不想胡雪岩非真有奇计雄略，经不住洋商的排挤，商事日渐中落，由盛转衰，终至破产，身败名裂。胡雪岩因而成为我国近代史中一奇特人物。
en: In The Red-Topped Merchant, Towers of Light, and other books, Gao Yang continues to draw on his extensive historical knowledge and accomplished storytelling to recount how Hu Xueyan’s wealth rose to its height after his beginnings in Shanghai and Hangzhou, and how he ultimately went bankrupt. These books describe Hu, by then a great merchant of Jiangsu and Zhejiang, transporting military funds and grain to help the Qing forces relieve the siege of Hangzhou. After the city falls, he turns to Zuo Zongtang as his patron, raising military funds, buying and transporting modern Western guns and artillery, borrowing immense sums from foreign merchants to support Zuo’s western campaigns, and assisting in his Western-style enterprises. Relying on official patronage, Hu then expands his power and comes to dominate commerce in Jiangsu and Zhejiang. His reputation spreads throughout the southeast. He is eventually granted the insignia of the second official rank and the privileges of wearing a yellow riding jacket and riding a horse inside the Forbidden City, becoming the only merchant of the late Qing to wear the red-topped official hat. Extravagant in the extreme and passionately fond of women, he builds splendid residences and gardens in Shanghai, Hangzhou, and elsewhere, surrounds himself with concubines, and delights in unrestrained debauchery. For more than a decade, his wealth and influence reach extraordinary heights. Yet Hu does not possess truly remarkable strategy or far-reaching ability. Unable to withstand the pressure of foreign merchants, his business gradually declines. Prosperity turns to ruin, until he is bankrupt and his reputation destroyed. He thus becomes one of the singular figures of China’s modern history.

zh: 高阳先生独具慧眼，落笔如神，情节曲折，人物如生，文字畅达，场景开阔，使一幅描绘动荡的晚清社会的画面，跃然纸上。
en: With a distinctive eye and an inspired pen, Gao Yang creates intricate plots, lifelike characters, fluent prose, and scenes of great scope, bringing a vivid picture of the turbulent society of the late Qing to the page.

zh: 欲知晚清巨贾胡雪岩由商而官、暴起暴落地过程，请见本公司出版的《红顶商人》和《灯火楼台》等书。
en: For the story of how Hu Xueyan, the great merchant of the late Qing, moved from commerce into official rank and rose and fell with such dramatic speed, see The Red-Topped Merchant, Towers of Light, and other titles published by our company.
